regime.headline: US yields remain elevated (10Y ~5%) and front-end pricing is hawkish, tightening conditions while broad credit/volatility confirmation is still unresolved.

regime.implication: Falling risk appetite from higher nominal and real yields is pressuring funding-sensitive sectors, but without canonical credit‑spread or volatility confirmation the market is best described as rates‑driven tightening rather than a broad risk‑off.
regime.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical MOVE/Treasury‑volatility and multi‑session IG/HY OAS time series showing persistent IG widening or a VIX/MOVE spike would materially shift this from a rates‑led tightening to broader market stress.

stories.title: Nominal/real yields are high while a governed 10Y term premium remains low
stories.whatChanged: US 10Y near 5.0% with 10Y real ~2.64% and NY Fed ACM term premium ~0.64% (10/22–10/23 canonical observations).
stories.whyItMatters: Elevated nominal and real yields tighten financial conditions even when term‑premium governance is low, raising funding costs for duration‑sensitive issuers.
stories.mechanism: Higher real yields and front‑end hawkish pricing (policy path) are pushing nominal yields up; a small governed term premium means supply/term‑premium forces are not the primary driver in current canonical evidence.
stories.conclusion: Current canonical evidence supports a rates‑led increase in funding costs driven largely by real‑rate/policy repricing rather than an outsized term‑premium shift.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Sustained rise in ACM term premium or auction/coverage evidence showing consistent demand failure would refute the policy/real‑rate dominance conclusion.

stories.title: Front‑end collateral and dealer data show slight dollar‑liquidity tightening
stories.whatChanged: 3M/6M T‑bill yields run ~+38bp above EFFR and dealer fails/net positions show material flows, indicating tighter front‑end collateral conditions.
stories.whyItMatters: Tighter front‑end/collateral elevates funding costs for banks and funding‑sensitive credit, which can amplify rates pressure into credit if persistent.
stories.mechanism: Bill‑to‑EFFR dislocation suggests collateral scarcity/tighter funding; dealer fails and net positions provide market‑structure context that could amplify rate moves into funding channels.
stories.conclusion: Canonical front‑end indicators point to mildly tighter dollar liquidity at the short end, a potential amplifier of rates pressure if sustained.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical cross‑currency basis and FX‑swap data showing ample offshore USD funding would weaken the tightness interpretation.

verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.
